components.name: Gluten-Risk Badge
components.description: Flags a recipe, shopping-list, or meal-card item that needs a verified gluten-free product. Appears on every page that can show one. components.name: Nav Bar
components.description: A plain hand-rolled two-row <nav> (src/App.tsx), not a Fluent navigation primitive. Row one: brand label plus the current page's own name, right-aligned. Row two: six links as an equal-width segmented control, each an icon over a visible Hungarian label, 44px tall. Client-side routing wired by hand on click; the active link carries aria-current="page". Selected state fills the whole segment with rgba(255,255,255,.14) and turns the icon/label full white — no border, no inset accent bar. Mobile-first: full-width segments at 360px, caps at max-width 480px and centers from bpLarge (640px) up.

components.name: Page Backdrop
components.description: The full-bleed dark/purple gradient every page's outer wrapper applies via the shared usePageBackdropStyles hook (src/styles/shell.ts) — one hook, one place, not re-declared per page. min-height: 100dvh ensures it fills the content column's height even on short pages. narrative.overview: Zero Gluten runs inside a dark navy/indigo chrome over a purple gradient backdrop — a register borrowed, user-pinned, from an unrelated enterprise dashboard reference. The product itself hasn't changed across any shell or page pass: it's still a plain-spoken kitchen companion, read one-handed, sometimes in a dim kitchen or a shop. Most real tasks — ingredient checklists, shopping checkboxes, the cook-today answer — still live on the same white, elevated cards this system built before any of the dark chrome existed; only the chrome and the page background around those cards went dark and colorful. Recipe Detail is the one deliberate exception: its content now sits directly on the backdrop, cardless, in the off-card light palette, with a meal-type-colored left accent standing in for the card edge every other page still uses. The nav has been rebuilt three times since this system's first pass: a two-tier top bar (brand strip over a link row) to a collapsible Fluent 2 NavDrawer left pane to a single horizontal icon-only bar to its current shape, a two-row bar (brand + current-page title, then a segmented icon-and-label control) spanning the full width, content routed below it. The dark/purple shell palette carried over unchanged across every rebuild; only the structure and the underlying markup changed. Visible labels returned in this pass (impeccable /live, an explicit "redesign... mobile-first" request), and the active route now fills its whole segment with a background rather than a thin border. The theme architecture itself stayed light (FluentProvider on zeroGlutenTheme, unchanged): the dark/purple treatment is hand-pinned hex applied only to chrome, page backgrounds, and — uniquely on Recipe Detail — the page's own body text, never inside a card elsewhere.
keyCharacteristics: Theme architecture is deliberately split: Fluent stays on the light theme; dark/purple is hand-pinned hex on chrome and backdrop, and (on Recipe Detail only) the page's own loose text, never inside a card elsewhere.

The nav is a hand-rolled two-row bar, not a Fluent navigation primitive — brand + current-page title on top, a segmented icon-and-label control below, client-side routing wired by hand on click. No responsive collapse, no overlay, traded deliberately for a bar that never needs to hide and reads at a glance.
Purple/indigo is the chrome/world color; rosemary green is demoted, not removed — it keeps its prior meaning inside cards.
Left-edge status stripes, not top strips — Catalog and Today's cards, and (at 6px, same width and hue family, as a border-left) Recipe Detail's cardless sections.

Recipe Detail is cardless by design, not by omission: header, macros, ingredients, and steps sit directly on the dark backdrop in the off-card palette, with a meal-type-colored left accent in place of the card edge. The gluten-risk badge and the glutenFreeNote callout are the sole exceptions.

Off-card text is a first-class concern: several real content elements, including the nav bar's own brand label and, in full now, Recipe Detail's entire body, sit directly on the dark backdrop and are individually checked against the rendered page, not assumed safe.

rules.name: The Always-Flagged Rule
rules.body: The gluten-risk-ingredient signal is reserved exclusively for that one meaning, on every page, regardless of color, backdrop, or whether the surrounding content sits in a card. Recipe Detail's gluten-risk badge and glutenFreeNote callout keep their filled backgrounds even though the rest of that page went cardless — this is the one deliberate exception to 'no filled background,' never the other way around. Codified in specs/constitution.md Principle 7.

rules.name: The One Hex, One Place Rule
rules.body: In-card colors stay in src/styles/colors.ts, shell/backdrop colors in src/styles/shellColors.ts, each imported everywhere needed, never re-declared locally.

rules.name: The Left-Border Reversal
rules.body: Left/right decorative card borders are a standing craft-floor ban in general, but meal-type color deliberately renders as a left-edge stripe or border-left — Catalog and Today's card rail, Recipe Detail's cardless-section accent — adopted from the user-pinned dark dashboard reference. The nest-cards-inside-cards ban is unaffected: stripes replace a color's position, they never become their own nested card, and Recipe Detail's accent replaces a card edge it no longer has, not a new card.

rules.name: The Check-The-Component's-Own-Defaults Rule
rules.body: A library component carries its own default styling from the active Fluent theme regardless of what backdrop it's dropped onto — composing one inside a hand-pinned dark surface requires explicitly overriding that default, not just adding new color on top. First caught on the (now-retired) NavDrawer's light-neutral background, by reading the rendered page's computed styles, not by reasoning about a className override in isolation.

dos: Do keep FluentProvider on the light theme — dark/purple styling is chrome-only (or, on Recipe Detail, page-body-only) hand-pinned hex, never a theme-level switch.
Do check every page's actual rendered output — including a library component's own computed styles — before trusting a written plan's survey.
Do keep the gluten-risk color and the three meal-type hues sourced from their one shared module each, regardless of position, backdrop, or card-vs-cardless treatment.
Do box genuinely dense content in its own white card rather than recoloring many individual text nodes, when a card is the chosen treatment for that surface.
Do keep the gluten-risk badge and glutenFreeNote boxed and filled even on a page that has otherwise gone cardless — the Always-Flagged Rule outranks any surface's own direction.
donts: Don't assume a page — or a drop-in component — has no contrast problem because nothing in the diff touched color; verify the real render.
Don't map the gluten-risk signal or any data-series hue to a UI framework's own semantic color token.

Don't carry forward a decorative distinction into a new structure just because it existed before — the old nav's violet 'tint' was dropped once already and has not earned its way back across two further nav rebuilds.
Don't give every list card treatment by default — Label checklist's flat list is a deliberate exception, and Recipe Detail's cardless body is now a second one.

Don't reach for decorative backdrop-filter/glass treatments on a card — Recipe Detail briefly carried a translucent, blurred 'glass' surface on its header/ingredients/step boxes; it matched no other page in the system and was removed in the same pass that made the page fully cardless.
Don't treat this file as a transition snapshot — the current nav bar and Recipe Detail's cardless treatment are each the one and only shipped state for their surface.
